### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Purkinje cells of the cerebellum receive direct input from climbing fibers. This is a well-established fact in neurobiology, as climbing fibers originate from the inferior olivary nucleus and form powerful excitatory synapses directly on Purkinje cells. Mossy fibers, on the other hand, provide indirect input to Purkinje cells by first synapsing with granule cells, which then send parallel fibers to synapse with Purkinje cells. Spinal neurons, neurons of the deep cerebellar nuclei, and pyramidal neurons of the cerebral cortex do not provide direct input to Purkinje cells.
